newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine spring sowing nearly complete-officials.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine spring sowing nearly complete-officials.

text.p: Ukraine's spring sowing campaign is nearly complete and crops are in a satisfactory condition, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Wednesday.

"Ukrainian farmers have sown 11.336 million hectares with all types of spring crops, compared to 9.829 million hectares at the same time last year," Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the ministry's crop department, told Reuters.
"The crops in all Ukrainian regions are growing in good and satisfactory condition," Tymoshenko added.
Government plans envisage Ukraine sowing 13.818 million hectares this spring to all types of crops.
Farmers have planted 4.446 million hectares with early spring grain, flat on year-ago levels.

Volodymyr Krut, deputy head of the Ukrainian Academy of Agrarian Sciences, said winter wheat was growing well in most parts of the country, but high temperatures in recent days could slow further growing of spring crops in the steppes of central and southern Ukraine.
Last autumn farmers sowed 8.24 million hectares with winter grains, mostly wheat.
Ukraine has forecast a grain harvest this year of 35 million tonnes compared to a record-low grain crop of 25.4 million tonnes in 1996.
Ukraine also planted 1.609 million hectares to sunflower with a forecast harvest of 2.3 million tonnes. At this time last year farmers had sown 1.467 million hectares to sunflower.
"There is no real danger to spring crops by now and we expect the usual May rains at the end of the month will provide extra moisture for plants," Krut added.
